text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 1.87% today, continuing a steep two-week slide of 9.3%. The immediate trigger appears to be oil prices moving lower—U.S. crude dropped below $104 per barrel as peace negotiations between the U.S. and Iran eased concerns about Middle Eastern supply disruptions. For a refiner, lower oil prices can pinch margins, since the company buys crude to process it into gasoline and diesel; when crude gets cheaper faster than refined products do, profit per barrel narrows. The timing also coincides with a leadership change at Marathon announced today, which may have added uncertainty as investors digest new management.

The stock's weakness fits a broader pattern affecting refiners this week. Refinery utilization is holding steady at a healthy 92.8%, but the industry faces headwinds: crude inventories are elevated at 693 million barrels, and market commentary suggests investors should remain cautious on Big Oil earnings reports given the gap between what companies earn and what guidance they provide going forward.
